review_limits: No paper draft was supplied, so claims-vs-code review was limited to claims inside the repository (README and documentation); paper claims could not be checked.

Recomputing all 17 SHA-256 hashes (66.8 GB) was sampled rather than executed end-to-end due to runtime constraints, though sampled hashes (e.g. data/mortality/temp.dta and data/links/derived/JW_matches_x2_unique_old.dta) matched byte-for-byte.
The Stata linkage and table-reproduction pipeline (run_machineB.do, ~4 hours) was not executed during this review.
The raw files that the upstream build tier would read (the unhashed raw census and matching inputs) remain unhashed on Machine B, as disclosed in replication/README.md.
The extraction script that produced data/truth/mlp_training1930_1940.dta from the MLP crosswalk archive remains outside the repository and could not be inspected.
structured_output.summary: No result-changing defect was found in this commit range. The commits introduce Machine B's input checksum generator (replication/hash_inputs_machineB.py) and manifest (replication/input_manifest_machineB.md), dynamically parsing all 17 preflighted data inputs from run_machineB.do and verifying them against disk. Data provenance entries in replication/README.md for the MLP truth crosswalk and CenSoc BUNMD files accurately reflect file metadata without overstating certainty.

verified_clean.evidence: replication/run_machineB.do:50-68 specifies 13 literal data files and 4 mortality variants. replication/hash_inputs_machineB.py:47-64 parses both literal lines and the foreach loop via regular expressions and enforces len(rels) == 17 (EXPECTED = 17), matching the 17 table entries in replication/input_manifest_machineB.md:11-27.
verified_clean.item: The generated manifest covers exactly the data inputs currently preflighted by Machine B.

verified_clean.evidence: replication/hash_inputs_machineB.py:37-45 extracts $REP_LINK dynamically from the ARTS-ECON-SHSRV block in replication/config.do:26-36, resolving to F:/Deaglan/Census_Transcriptions without hardcoding machine-specific drive letters in the script logic.
verified_clean.item: Dynamic root path resolution from repository configuration.

verified_clean.evidence: All 17 data files exist on disk under F:/Deaglan/Census_Transcriptions/data/. Sampled inputs (data/mortality/temp.dta and data/links/derived/JW_matches_x2_unique_old.dta) were independently hashed with hashlib.sha256 and matched the values in replication/input_manifest_machineB.md:14,23 (2223ed... and 594be0...).
verified_clean.item: File existence and SHA-256 digest integrity on disk.

verified_clean.evidence: replication/hash_inputs_machineB.py:85-113 recomputes hashes and tracks mismatches against read_manifest(). In --check mode, line 112 calls sys.exit(1 if changed else 0) before reaching the manifest write step at lines 128-129.
verified_clean.item: Checksum verification mode (--check) is strictly read-only and halts with non-zero exit code on discrepancies.

verified_clean.evidence: replication/hash_inputs_machineB.py:83-84 guards execution with socket.gethostname().upper() != 'ARTS-ECON-SHSRV', and lines 89-91 abort immediately if any of the 17 inputs are missing on disk.
verified_clean.item: Hostname and input validation guards prevent invalid runs.

verified_clean.evidence: replication/README.md:80-81 documents the IPUMS MLP crosswalk (mlp_census_crosswalk_v2_0.stata.zip) and truth set (mlp_training1930_1940.dta) with dates 2026-02-10 and 2026-08-18, and CenSoc BUNMD files with date 2025-11-14. Verified directly against filesystem timestamps in F:\Deaglan\Census_Transcriptions\data\truth\ and F:\Deaglan\Census_Transcriptions\data\mortality\raw\.
verified_clean.item: Provenance documentation and file modification dates in README match filesystem metadata.

verified_clean.evidence: git diff f389a74~1..HEAD modifies only replication/README.md, replication/hash_inputs_machineB.py, and replication/input_manifest_machineB.md; no Stata estimation or linkage code in LINKAGE/code/ or CODE/ was modified.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
